notes: Read SKILL.md in full (single-file skill, 935 lines). The skill covers eBPF observability: kernel prerequisites, bpftrace/bcc install, Cilium with Hubble, Tetragon TracingPolicies (process, file, egress, privilege-escalation, container-escape, file-integrity), bpftrace one-liners, Prometheus/ebpf_exporter/Grafana integration, Parca/Pyroscope profiling and troubleshooting with bpftool.

Medium: following it has the agent run sudo apt/dnf installs, mount bpffs and set sysctl, helm-install Cilium (with kubeProxyReplacement=true, which replaces cluster networking), Tetragon, ebpf_exporter, Parca and Pyroscope, kubectl-apply TracingPolicies that include Sigkill enforcement (restrict-egress kills processes connecting to 169.254.169.254, SKILL.md:243-273; init_module Sigkill, SKILL.md:683-687), and download CLI tarballs into /usr/local/bin with sudo. Acceptable because these are the documented setup steps for the user's own cluster and hosts, the bpftrace one-liners are read-only tracing, and nothing is sent to third parties (the SIEM forwarder at SKILL.md:736 targets a placeholder siem.internal).

Review before running: the Cilium and Hubble CLIs are fetched at an unpinned version resolved from stable.txt and the tetra CLI from releases/latest (SKILL.md:111-120, 175-177) without checksum verification; FlameGraph is git-cloned unpinned and its Perl scripts executed (SKILL.md:788-790); the btfhub archive is wget'd (SKILL.md:855). These are official vendor release artifacts, not scripts piped to a shell, but pin versions and verify checksums. Installing Cilium with kube-proxy replacement and applying Sigkill policies changes cluster behavior — confirm with the user and test outside production first. Parca is configured with store.insecure=true and debuginfo upload (SKILL.md:757-759), suitable only for an in-cluster store. Some kprobe names (__x64_sys_*, dns_resolve) are kernel- and arch-specific.
